text:
Tara: Ran a sensitivity sweep this morning to see how prefill/prefix cache hits affect continuous-batcher formation. noticed some strange underfill at certain loads.
Mike: short version — underfill = lower throughput + p95 spike? can you paste numbers? :thinking_face:
Tara: yep. baseline (no cache): throughput 520 tok/s, p95 78ms. with prefill cache enabled (real workloads, ~45% hits) throughput drops to 410 tok/s, p95 120ms. CPU/GPU utilization also lower.
Ash: that screams microbatch underfill rather than a kernel perf bug. any change in virtual_len distribution?
Tara: exactly — virtual_len shifted left. median virtual_len went from 64 -> 22. histogram attached in perf-bot output below.
perf-bot: sweep summary:
```
config: prefill_cache: on
workload: mix-prod-3
samples: 120
median_virtual_len: 22
p95_lat_ms: 120
throughput_tok_s: 410
kernel_choice_breakdown:
  - fused-attn-64: 35%
  - slow-small-threads: 55%
  - fallback: 10%
notes: kernel flip happens when virtual_len < 28 for this model+hw
```
Mike: kernel_choice_breakdown is the key. if cache hits reduce the virtual length below the kernel threshold we end up on a slower codepath.
Julia: can we move the kernel threshold or add a virtual_len-aware admission tweak so we batch a few more live requests instead of dispatching small microbatches? maybe a short stall (<2ms).
Tara: tried a simple stall of 2ms in the admission policy — p95 improved to 95ms but tail got noisy at high qps. throughput recovered to 480 tok/s.
Ryan: what about token budget target change? bumping target from 256->384 for live admission might keep virtual_len > threshold more often.
Ash: token budget bump helps but increases latency variance for single-request flows. we should weigh throughput vs worst-case latency.
Mike: can we pick kernel differently? i.e., if virtual_len is 22, still prefer fused-attn-64 kernel for that batch even if it's suboptimal per-op? might be cheaper overall due to reduced overhead.
Tara: tried forcing fused-attn-64 for virtual_len 20..28 — throughput improved, p95 ~85ms. but we saw higher GPU peak memory in some traces; possible register spilling for some model shapes.
Julia: here's a config snippet I prototyped — admission policy + kernel preference heuristic:
```
admission:
  stall_ms: 1.5
  token_budget_target: 320
kernel_pref:
  prefer_fused_if_virtual_len_ge: 16
```
Ash: nice. we should add a small safety: if kernel_pref leads to >90% memory occupancy then fallback to default.
Tara: agreed. also found perf regression after last kernel-selection tweak on commit 6f2a — that change tightened selection purely on per-op FLOPS which doesn't account for KV-cache prefix overhead.
perf-bot: recent commit impact (6f2a -> current): +18% p95 for cache-heavy mixes, kernel selection mismatch events +2300/min.
Mike: ok action items:
  - (Tara) roll config above into a canary on one serving pool and capture traces (latency/virtual_len/kernel)
  - (Ash) add mem-occupancy guard on forced kernel pref
  - (Julia) run sensitivity grid for stall_ms ∈ {0,0.5,1,1.5,2.0} and token_budget ∈ {256,320,384}
  - (Ryan) repro commit 6f2a regression and add a unit test for kernel-selection w/ prefix cache enabled
Tara: starting canary now on pool-rc-3. link to dashboard: http://perf.redwood/internal/runs/2509876543
Mike: ping me when traces are in. I'll help analyze kernel-level traces (smoke perf counters + CU occupancy).
Ash: quick note — this pattern only shows on long-prefill models (prefill 512+) and when hit-rate ∈ [30..60%]. low-hit (<10%) or nearly-all-hit (>90%) are fine.
Julia: thanks — will post grid results by EOD.
Tara: thanks everyone. follow-ups in thread. :white_check_mark:
